text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

- Work on the rail tunnel linking the Norwegian capital to Oslo's new international airport at Gardemoen was halted on Monday due to a disagreement between the partners over payment. Gardemoen is due to take over from Fornebu as the main airport next year.
- The postal services' losses due to robberies amounted to a record low 929,000 crowns last year, while postal workers are believed to have stolen about 2.8 million crowns.
- Swedish power producer Vattenfall wants to increase its share in the Norwegian market. Fredrikstad Energiverk could be the first Norwegian electricity producer to be bought by the Swedish giant.
- Construction and engineering group Kvaerner ASA is considering buying a shipyard in the United States.

- The Conservative party's proposals to cut taxes could increase pressure in the Norwegian economy with faster price growth and higher interest rates, says chief economist Nils Terje Furunes at Sparebanken NOR.

- It is likely that Den norske Bank (DnB) will win the takeover battle with Fokus Bank for mortgage lender BNbank. From an economic view, however, Fokus could have the best offer. Many other parties may make an offer for the niche lender, but Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse is unlikely to join in the fight.
